items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: It was Glass. Oh, yeah. And the Glass, you know, Booker T. It was Booker T's job. We played out there about three or four times.

ctx.x: Got very good reviews too. Another fellow in the New York Times wrote that he thought you were about the best client player. Yeah. I think that's what he said, something like that.

Yeah, that's right. I want to ask you about Bob Lyons too. He had a band? Yeah, he had a band. You play with him much? Well, I played with him a little. Not long. But not with his group that he had when he hadn't been in. I don't know what had happened, but he just got a line up together. Little old boy he was playing, drum. I don't remember the other fellas than he had. But I didn't play but a few jobs with him. I see. And Baras, did you play many jobs with him? No, Baras? No, Baras. I only played a few times…

I notice now that- This was a good siren or trumpet. I notice now how most of the clarinet players around aren't as loud as you are. Back in the old days, would you say that you were louder than most of the clarinet players or were there a lot of them who can play as strong as you can?
